stories.headline: Students at More Than 180 Colorado Schools Expected to Walk Out Friday to Protest ICE
stories.summary:
Students from over 180 schools across Colorado are set to walk out of class Friday as part of a statewide "ICE Out" protest against U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement actions, according to organizers with the Colorado Youth Coalition and 50501 Colorado. In Denver, protesters are scheduled to gather at La Alma-Lincoln Park at noon.

The walkout spans students in Adams, Arapahoe, Alamosa, Boulder, Broomfield, Mesa, Morgan, Denver, Douglas, El Paso, Garfield, Jefferson, Larimer, Montrose, Montezuma, Pueblo, Teller and Weld counties. Mountain Vista High School senior Braeden Kieffer said students in Douglas County are also protesting the use of Flock surveillance cameras in their community.

Cherry Creek School District notified families Thursday that it does not endorse walkouts but supports students' First Amendment rights. Boulder Valley School District said it is preparing for likely protests at high schools and will focus on student safety and minimizing disruption.

A similar ICE Out protest in January drew thousands of Colorado students and community members, and prompted some schools to cancel or delay classes after a wave of teacher absences. Denver Public Schools has previously challenged federal immigration policy through legal action.

stories.headline: Gov. Polis Appoints Ken Salazar as Special Envoy to Resolve San Luis Valley Ranch Dispute
stories.summary:
Gov. Jared Polis has signed an executive order appointing former U.S. Interior Secretary and Colorado Attorney General Ken Salazar as a "special envoy" tasked with resolving a long-running dispute between billionaire ranch owner William Harrison and heirs of an 1844 Spanish land grant in the San Luis Valley. Salazar, 71, is directed to facilitate conversations and form a recommendation on the conflict over the roughly 83,000-acre Cielo Vista Ranch in Costilla County.

The dispute centers on the Sangre de Cristo Land Grant, which predates Colorado statehood and guaranteed settlers rights to hunt, graze livestock and gather timber on the land. Harrison, who purchased the ranch in 2017, began constructing an 8-foot fence around the property in 2020, which was halted after about 20 miles were erected following a temporary injunction.

An 83-page report released this summer found the fence potentially harmful to wildlife including federally listed Canada lynx and silverspot butterflies, as well as deer, elk, eagles and cutthroat trout. In a separate court ruling in May, land grant heirs won the right to continue grazing livestock on the property but lost the right to collect firewood in a buffer zone around Harrison's improvements.

"We can and must do better than eternal litigation and conflict," Polis said in a news release. Salazar, a native of the San Luis Valley, said he planned to listen closely and ask the right questions in his new role.

stories.headline: Denver7 Investigation: Security Company Accused of Using Illegal Police Lights, Montana Registration Loophole
stories.summary:
A Denver7 Investigates report has found that Denver Metro Security, a local company providing traffic control at construction sites across the metro area, has been operating vehicles with Montana license plates and using red and blue emergency lights without proper permits, in violation of state law, according to Colorado State Patrol.

Colorado State Trooper Hunter Matthews told Denver7 the situation is "very black and white" and that red and blue lights can only be legally used on vehicles registered to law enforcement or government agencies, or those with a specific emergency vehicle equipment authorization from the state. The Colorado Department of Motor Vehicles confirmed Denver Metro Security does not hold such an authorization.

Former company contractor Kevin Heely and former sales director Dwight Berry both came forward to dispute claims by the company's operations manager, Nate Boyd, who had previously told Denver7 the company had permission to use the lights. Berry alleged the company has been misleading clients and the public, and said it "thinks they're above the law."

Denver residents working near construction sites have expressed concern about armed guards in uniform operating vehicles with law enforcement-style lights that have no clear official authority. Denver7 said it spent weeks tracking the company's vehicles at multiple job sites before publishing its findings.

stories.headline: Colorado Parks and Wildlife Crews Clear 100-Yard Logjam on Arkansas River Ahead of Labor Day
stories.summary:
Colorado Parks and Wildlife crews cleared an unprecedented 100-yard logjam that had completely blocked the surface of the Arkansas River near Hecla Junction, between Buena Vista and Salida, in time for the Labor Day holiday weekend. The jam, composed of tree trunks up to 20 inches in diameter cemented together with pine needles and mud, was washed into the river by heavy rainstorms on Aug. 22.

After allowing the river's natural force to reduce the jam from 100 yards to about 20 yards over several days, CPW sent boat crews with hand tools, long poles and paddles to finish the job. The debris was cleared gradually through steady chipping and redirecting of logs rather than a sudden unplugging, said Arkansas Headwaters park manager Tom Waters.

CPW clarified that despite dozens of public suggestions, the agency possesses neither explosives nor pyrotechnic expertise to blast the jam free. Crews subsequently floated the rapids downstream to confirm no major logs had snagged again farther along the river.

"It was like a weight lifted off all of our shoulders," said CPW officer Connor Dady. The jam clearance comes alongside other challenges on the Arkansas, including a major sewage spill from Pueblo stretching 100 miles downstream to Las Animas that has raised health and agriculture concerns in the Lower Arkansas region.

stories.headline: Single-Engine Plane Crashes in San Juan Mountains Near Telluride; Search and Rescue Deployed
stories.summary:
Search and rescue crews were deployed Thursday evening after a single-engine plane crashed in a remote area of the San Juan Mountains near Telluride, according to the San Miguel County Sheriff's Office. A 911 call reporting smoke near Dolores Peak, about 15 miles southwest of Telluride, came in at 3:22 p.m., and first responders confirmed the crash site just after 7 p.m. after a multi-hour trek to the remote location.

Denver air traffic controllers contacted San Miguel County emergency dispatch about a missing airplane shortly after the smoke was first reported, though officials had not confirmed as of Thursday evening whether the missing plane and the crash were the same aircraft. Helicopter crews were being dispatched to determine if anyone survived.

The crash site was on the north side of Dolores Peak, in rugged terrain that slowed the response of ground crews including sheriff's deputies, Telluride Fire and the Bureau of Land Management. No information on the number of people aboard or the origin and destination of the flight had been released.

stories.headline: Nob Hill Inn, Downtown Denver's Last Historic Dive Bar, Faces Sept. 30 Closure Without Fundraising Help
stories.summary:
Nob Hill Inn, a nearly century-old dive bar on East Colfax Avenue and the last of its kind in downtown Denver, is facing closure by Sept. 30 unless it can raise enough money to cover mounting debts and repair costs. New operator Christy Simonsen, who took over this week from longtime owner John Plessinger — who ran the bar since 1969 — said the establishment owes approximately $79,000 and is dealing with plumbing problems, a deteriorating floor and a damaged roof.

Simonsen and supporters attribute much of the business decline to the ongoing East Colfax Avenue Bus Rapid Transit construction project, which has blocked sidewalk access, eliminated parking and diverted pedestrian traffic. Multiple other businesses along the corridor, including Enzo's End pizzeria, Misfit Snack Bar and Colfax and Cream, have also closed or cited the BRT construction as a factor in revenue losses.

A GoFundMe campaign launched Tuesday by bar regular Brittani Trujillo aims to raise $15,000, having collected roughly $2,000 from nearly 40 donors as of Thursday. Simonsen said the bar has been denied city loans because it earns just enough to be disqualified from assistance programs.

Simonsen is hosting a public forum Saturday starting around 4 or 5 p.m. to gather ideas and community support. Plessinger declined to sell to outside buyers, insisting only Simonsen take over to preserve the bar's longtime character and atmosphere.

stories.headline: Former Broncos Cornerback Alphonso Smith Jr. Dies at 40
stories.summary:
Former Denver Broncos cornerback Alphonso Smith Jr. has died at age 40, the Palm Beach County Medical Examiner's Office confirmed to the Denver Post on Thursday. TMZ reported that Smith died by suicide Wednesday at a housing community in Pahokee, Fla., where he grew up. The Medical Examiner's Office and Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office declined to provide further details.

The Broncos selected Smith with the 37th overall pick in the 2009 NFL Draft, trading their 2010 first-round pick to the Seattle Seahawks in the process. Seattle used the resulting pick — 14th overall — to select future All-Pro safety Earl Thomas, while Smith played just one season in Denver without starting a game, recording 14 tackles before being traded to the Detroit Lions for tight end Dan Gronkowski.

Smith played three seasons in Detroit, starting 11 games and recording five interceptions in 2010 and three in 2011, before being released in 2012. He later returned to Pahokee, where he briefly served as head football coach at his alma mater before being removed following allegations of inappropriate conduct.

Smith faced a domestic battery charge in 2016, and Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office records show approximately 19 incident reports involving him between 1999 and 2025. He was 40 years old at the time of his death.

stories.headline: Labor Day Weekend Weather: Warm Temperatures, Scattered Storms Expected Across Denver Metro
stories.summary:
Denver is forecast to see unseasonably warm temperatures through the Labor Day holiday weekend, with increasing chances for scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms as monsoon moisture returns to the region. Storm chances are expected to be highest Sunday and Monday, with a more active pattern of daily afternoon storms projected to continue into next week.

Denver International Airport is bracing for a busy travel period, with more than 368,000 passengers expected to pass through security checkpoints from Thursday through Monday — roughly the same volume as last year's Labor Day weekend. Airport officials have urged travelers to plan accordingly for potential weather-related delays.

stories.headline: Boulder County Enacts Stage 2 Fire Restrictions for Western Areas as Wildfire Risk Persists
stories.summary:
Boulder County has enacted Stage 2 fire restrictions for western portions of the county and Stage 1 restrictions for eastern areas amid ongoing wildfire concerns across Colorado heading into the Labor Day weekend. The tiered restrictions reflect differing levels of fire risk between the drier, more forested western terrain and the eastern plains.

Stage 2 restrictions typically prohibit all open burning, including campfires, charcoal grills and fireworks, and may restrict other fire-risk activities. The restrictions come as CPR News continues to track multiple active wildfires across Colorado on its 2026 wildfire map. Boulder County government offices will be closed Monday, Sept. 7, in observance of Labor Day.

stories.headline: Labor Day Weekend Events: Jazz Aspen, Arvada Powwow, Colfax Canvas Mural Festival Among Top Colorado Activities
stories.summary:
Colorado residents have a range of events to choose from over the Labor Day weekend. The Jazz Aspen Snowmass Labor Day Experience runs Sept. 4-6 at Snowmass Town Park, featuring Benson Boone, Tim McGraw, Bonnie Raitt and Shaboozey, among others. Wings Over the Rockies hosts Warbird Weekend at Centennial Airport on Sept. 5-6, showcasing WWII-era aircraft with ground tours and flight experiences.

In the Denver metro area, the Arvada Center and Rocky Mountain Indian Chamber of Commerce are hosting a free all-day Arvada Powwow on Saturday, Sept. 5, celebrating Native American culture, art, food and dance. Denver Union Station and the Mexican Cultural Center are kicking off Hispanic Heritage Month with Ritmo & Raíces on Sunday, Sept. 6, featuring live music, dance and bilingual tours from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m.

The sixth annual Colfax Canvas mural festival continues through the weekend along East Colfax Avenue in Aurora, culminating Friday with an art walk featuring new murals, gallery openings, food and live music at eight venues starting at 5 p.m. The Windsor Harvest Festival also runs Sept. 5-7 with hot-air balloons, a parade and fireworks over Windsor Lake.

stories.headline: Denver Summit FC Hosts Gotham FC in NWSL Action Sunday at Home
stories.summary:
Denver Summit FC, the city's newest professional sports franchise, returns to home action Sunday when it hosts Gotham FC in a National Women's Soccer League match. The game gives Denver-area soccer fans another opportunity to see the expansion club compete at home during its inaugural season.

Denver Summit FC has drawn community interest as the NWSL continues to expand its footprint in major markets. Details on kickoff time and venue were not provided in available event listings, but organizers encouraged fans to attend as the club builds its local following heading into the latter portion of the season.

stories.headline: Two Tallest Buildings in Colorado Springs Set for Foreclosure Auction Beginning Oct. 21
stories.summary:
The two tallest buildings in Colorado Springs are headed to a foreclosure auction beginning Oct. 21, according to El Paso County records. The Colorado Sun reported the development as part of a broader look at economic challenges facing commercial real estate in the region.

Details on the specific buildings, their owners and the debt behind the foreclosure proceedings were not fully disclosed in available reporting, but the auction of the city's two most prominent towers marks a significant commercial real estate event for Colorado's second-largest city. The outcome could affect tenants, lenders and the broader Colorado Springs downtown business district.

weekendEvents.description: Latin rock icons Maná return to Red Rocks for the first of two Labor Day weekend performances. The Grammy-winning Mexican band is known for songs including 'Rayando el Sol,' 'Oye Mi Amor' and 'Labios Compartidos.'

weekendEvents.description: Phish opens its annual Labor Day weekend run at Dick's Sporting Goods Park. Known for improvisational performances where no two shows are exactly alike, the band's Colorado appearances have become one of the state's most anticipated end-of-summer traditions.
weekendEvents.location: Dick's Sporting Goods Park, Commerce City

weekendEvents.description: The Colorado Symphony presents a cello ensemble performance at Boettcher Concert Hall in downtown Denver.

weekendEvents.description: Connecticut duo Have a Nice Life performs at the Gothic Theatre. The band is known for its atmospheric blend of post-punk, shoegaze, industrial and experimental rock, with the acclaimed album Deathconsciousness remaining a cornerstone of its catalog.

weekendEvents.title: First Friday Art Walk
weekendEvents.description: September's First Friday Art Walk spans the Art District on Santa Fe, RiNo ArtPark and other Denver neighborhoods, featuring food trucks, local artisan vendors, live music and gallery shows.

weekendEvents.description: A multi-day showcase exploring the diversity of performing arts, theater and cultural expression in Denver and beyond. The event includes artisan vendors displaying and selling crafts and cultural merchandise.

weekendEvents.title: Gareth Emery at Mission Ballroom
weekendEvents.description: British electronic music producer and DJ Gareth Emery takes over Mission Ballroom for a Saturday night performance. Emery has spent years moving between trance, progressive and vocal-driven electronic music.

weekendEvents.title: Christone 'Kingfish' Ingram at Bluebird Theater
weekendEvents.description: Grammy-winning blues guitarist Christone 'Kingfish' Ingram brings his explosive guitar playing to the Bluebird Theater. Ingram has earned a reputation as one of the leading voices helping bring blues to a new generation.

weekendEvents.title: Boulder Art Festival
weekendEvents.description: More than 100 artists from Colorado and across the country display and sell their work along Pearl Street Mall in downtown Boulder over two days.

weekendEvents.title: Saint Rafka Lebanese and Middle Eastern Festival
weekendEvents.description: A two-day festival in Lakewood celebrating Lebanese and Middle Eastern culture, food and traditions.

weekendEvents.title: Bright Nights at Four Mile
weekendEvents.description: A multi-night outdoor event at Four Mile Historic Park in Denver, running through September 6 as part of a late-summer series.

topStory.headline: Trump Administration Asks Supreme Court to Reinstate USPS Mail Ballot Rules Blocked by Federal Judge
topStory.summary:
The Trump administration filed an emergency appeal with the U.S. Supreme Court on Thursday seeking to immediately reinstate new U.S. Postal Service regulations governing mail-in ballots, after a federal judge temporarily blocked the rules from taking effect. The administration's filing came as U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani was preparing to rule on whether to extend her block on the regulations, which are set to expire Sept. 10.

The new USPS rules, issued following an executive order by President Donald Trump, would require states to submit voter names, home addresses, and unique barcodes for every mail-in ballot distributed. Postal workers would then deliver ballots only to voters whose information appears on the state-provided list. Solicitor General D. John Sauer argued in the Supreme Court filing that the rules impose only 'modest' ballot design and review requirements and that regulation of the U.S. mail — not federal elections — is 'plainly constitutional.' Sauer also warned that delay increases the risk that some states will miss compliance deadlines before ballots are printed for the November 2026 midterm elections.

Judge Talwani sided with a coalition of Democratic-led states and voting rights groups when she issued her temporary restraining order, finding that the USPS rule likely unlawfully usurped states' authority to administer their own elections — power that she said would require congressional approval to override. She noted that most states have already ordered their mail ballots and face an 'impossible' timeline to comply, with the November election roughly two months away. A whistleblower separately told Congress that the requirements could result in large numbers of mail ballots never being sent.

Decades of legal precedent establish that election administration in the United States is primarily a state responsibility. Dozens of Democratic state attorneys general filed suit against the administration after an earlier legal challenge was turned away by the Supreme Court, which at that time ruled the case was premature because the regulations had not yet been finalized. The states challenging the USPS rule have until Tuesday, Sept. 8, to formally respond to the administration's Supreme Court application before the justices decide whether to act.
